summary_paragraph: A female patient with end-stage renal disease, antiphospholipid syndrome, and a history of recurrent hyperkalemia was admitted for weakness, dizziness, and paresthesias. She had recently started baclofen for muscle spasms and took two 10mg doses before experiencing prolonged sleep and new neurological symptoms. In the emergency department, her potassium was 6.7 mEq/L (non-hemolyzed), prompting treatment with calcium gluconate and urgent hemodialysis. Her symptoms were attributed to both hyperkalemia and the sedative effects of baclofen combined with Dilaudid. She underwent multiple dialysis sessions, with potassium normalizing to 4.8 mEq/L. A right heart catheterization revealed improved pulmonary pressures, leading to an increase in her dry weight goal by 2kg to prevent excessive fluid removal. An ultrasound of the left leg showed no deep vein thrombosis despite tenderness. Due to persistent dizziness and safety concerns at home, she was discharged to an extended care rehabilitation facility with follow-up planned with neurology and instructions to monitor weight and INR.
problems: Adverse effect of antiparkinsonism drugs and other central muscle-tone depressants
